title: Abroad: where a new English channel should aim

review.verdict: Mostly sound. 'US first, UAE out' holds, mainly on population.
notes: 30 points raised; the ones marked must-fix are corrected on this page.
Corrected: the claim that Canada, the UK and Australia are keener than the US. True for tarot only.
Corrected: two UK survey lines and the UAE law wording, to match what the sources say.
Corrected: ad price is a cost for this page, not a benefit.
Corrected: state groups now match the numbers; Florida is about the middle, not above it.
Added on the reviewer's advice: payment companies' rules, New York's fortune-telling law, and the three search words on one scale.
Still open: the fixes themselves have not had a second review. The reviewer could not open the Tarotoo article or Meta's full policy text.

verdict: If the new channel is in English for Western viewers, aim it at the United States first: it has by far the most people, and the strongest interest in Akashic and healing among large countries. The same reels also reach Canada, the United Kingdom and Australia, which are keener than the US on tarot and less keen on Akashic and healing. Do not aim at the UAE. Two things must be settled before this is final: how buyers abroad will pay, and which audience the channel is for.
how: Interest numbers are Google Trends, read on 21 Nov 2026 in the built-in browser: past 12 months, web search, English search terms 'tarot reading', 'akashic records' and 'energy healing'. Each number is interest per person inside that place, on a 0 to 100 scale where 100 is the top place for that word. It is not the number of searches, it only counts people who search in English, and each word is scaled by itself, so a 59 for tarot cannot be compared with a 94 for Akashic.

countries.name: United States
countries.line: By far the most people, and the strongest large country for Akashic.
facts: 30% of US adults consult astrology, tarot or a fortune teller at least once a year; tarot alone is 11%
Pew Research, survey of 9,593 adults, Oct 2024
Nearly a quarter of adults aged 18 to 29 use tarot at least yearly; 3% of those 65 and over
Pew Research, Oct 2024
Psychic services industry: 2.3 billion dollars a year, about 105,000 people working in it
IBISWorld figures, as carried in an AP news report, May 2025
55.8% of tarot.com's desktop visits came from the US; Canada 4.8%, UK 4.7%, India 4.2%, Australia 3.3%. One US website's traffic, not a market share.
Similarweb, Dec 2025

New York makes fortune telling for a fee a class B misdemeanour unless it is a show 'solely for the purpose of entertainment or amusement'. Bills to repeal it were filed in 2025. Other states and towns have their own rules.
New York Penal Law 165.35, NY Senate site
countries.care: Most Americans who do this say it is for fun. Some states restrict paid fortune telling. See 'Who is serious' and 'Take care' below.

countries.name: Canada
countries.line: Second large country for Akashic, after the US. Shares the US clocks.
facts: 20% of Canadians have consulted a psychic and 11% a medium. The survey asked this as ways people had tried to contact the dead.
Ipsos for Blue Ant Media, 1,001 adults, May 2021
Nearly half of Canadians, and a majority of women, believe some people have psychic powers
Angus Reid Institute, 1,515 adults, 2016 (old)
Inside Canada: British Columbia 100, Alberta 98, Manitoba 97, Ontario 92, Quebec 45
Google Trends 'tarot reading', 21 Nov 2026
countries.care: Quebec reads low on the English word, most likely because it searches in French (not measured).

countries.name: United Kingdom
countries.line: Tarot is strong. Akashic and healing are weaker here than in North America.
facts: 23% of Britons have consulted a psychic or medium: 12% with serious intent, 11% only for fun. 57% of those who went thought the psychic was truthful.
YouGov, 2,500 adults, Sept 2011 (old), as summarised by British Religion in Numbers
30% of Britons see telepathy as plausible, 30% reiki, 17% crystal healing
YouGov, July 2025
Inside the UK: England 100, Wales 89, Scotland 84, Northern Ireland 76
Google Trends 'tarot reading', 21 Nov 2026
countries.care: UK advertising rules: the seller must be able to prove a claim. No claims about how accurate a reading is, no promises to improve health or wealth or break curses, and healing only as spiritual, never physical.

countries.name: Australia
countries.line: High on all three words. Small country.
facts: 37% of Australians have had a mystical or supernatural experience or know someone who has
Australian Community Survey 2019, as reported by Australian Women's Weekly
38% of Gen Z Australians call themselves spiritual
ANU Gen Z study, reported May 2024

Inside Australia the states are close: Western Australia 55, Queensland 53, Victoria 50, South Australia 50, New South Wales 46, Tasmania 42. Northern Territory read 100 and is left out: about 250,000 people, the same small-place quirk as Wyoming.
Google Trends 'tarot reading', 21 Nov 2026
countries.care: Its evening is early afternoon in India, the opposite end of the day from the US.

countries.name: New Zealand
countries.line: Keen but tiny. Comes along with Australia.

countries.name: Ireland
countries.line: Highest real country for 'energy healing'. Comes along with the UK.
countries.care: Akashic read 44 or lower here, or had no data: it was outside the top 22 places.

countries.name: Singapore
countries.line: Read 100 for 'akashic records', level with the US within the noise. English, small.
facts: About 4.6 lakh overseas Indians live in Singapore
MEA figures as reported by NewsX, 2025

countries.name: United Arab Emirates
countries.people: about 10 million, of whom about 39 lakh are Indians
countries.line: Do not target. UAE law punishes sorcery and quackery, and local guides say that covers fortune-telling and promoting it online.
facts: Article 366 of Federal Decree-Law 31 of 2021 punishes illusion, sorcery or quackery done to exploit or harm others, and promoting it by any means
Khaleej Times report of the public prosecution's notice
Seven people were jailed and fined AED 50,000 for sorcery
Khaleej Times; Arabian Business
A UAE law firm's guide says claiming to see the future and promoting fortune-telling, in person or online, are covered
askthelaw.ae (a guide, not the law text; it does not name tarot)
countries.care: This is a precaution, not legal advice. Other Gulf countries probably carry similar risk; they were not checked. Followers from the Gulf may arrive by themselves; do not sell readings there or run ads there without a lawyer's view. Interest numbers: Akashic was outside the top 22 places.

countries.name: Europe and Latin America in other languages
countries.people: France, Spain, Germany, Brazil, Mexico, Argentina
countries.line: Tarot is big, but in Spanish, French, German and Portuguese. A later channel, not this one.
facts: A tarot trade report puts Germany at 7% and Brazil at 6% of world tarot card sales, after the US (38%) and UK (12%)
Deckaura 2026 report (a seller's own estimate)
Ad prices in Brazil, Mexico and Argentina are 1.4 to 4.8 dollars per thousand views, against 10.5 to 16.8 in the US
Stackmatix 2026 table (no source named)
countries.care: Our English search words cannot measure these places, so no interest number is shown.

ad_note: Ad price = what it costs an advertiser to buy 1,000 ad views in that country, in US dollars. For this page it is a cost: reaching Americans with paid ads is the dearest of all. It is only a loose sign of spending power, and it is not money Instagram pays the page. Figures are for Facebook, from Stackmatix's 2026 table, which names no data source and says Instagram runs 15 to 25% higher. India on the same table is 0.8 to 2.4.

who_pays.note: The catch in the US numbers: most people do this for fun. Pew did not ask who pays. Our reading is that buyers come from the smaller group who do it for insight.
tiles: do it mainly for helpful insight
lean on it at least a little for big life decisions (Pew's chart; its text gives 1% a lot and 5% a little)
groups: 43% believe in astrology, against 27% of women 50 and over
17% come for insight; nearly a quarter use tarot yearly
33% use tarot yearly (9% of others); 29% come for insight
15% see a fortune teller yearly (3% of White Americans)
12%, 11% and 9% lean on these practices for big decisions (4% of White Americans)
who_pays.source: Pew Research Center, survey of 9,593 US adults, Oct 2024, published May 2025

price.note: A handful of public listings found by search on 21 Nov 2026. Not a price survey.

30 minute tarot audio call, prices as listed

states.note: You cannot choose states when you post a reel. States matter for three things: which US clock to post on, what life the reels should picture, and where to point paid tests later. Small states jump around in these numbers, so read this as a rough picture, not a ranking.

big.title: Where the most people are
big.source: The four most populous states. A tarot app's own study (Tarotoo, April 2026, reported by CW33) also names California, New York and Texas as the top three for tarot interest; its headline counts looked too high to trust and are not used here.

states.glitch: Wyoming read 100 for tarot, 82 for Akashic and 100 for energy healing, with under 600,000 people. On healing the next state reads 26, which cannot be real, so Wyoming is left out and no healing ranking is shown. The same weakness touches other small states: Idaho at 100, Vermont and Alaska lead the Akashic list on very few searches. Treat the Akashic list as weak.
clusters: 45 and 46 for tarot, where the middle state reads about 35. Akashic 34, about the middle.
Oregon, Nevada, New Mexico, Hawaii, Colorado
41 to 51 for tarot, and the same states sit high on the Akashic list. Pacific and Mountain clocks.
Vermont, Maine, Rhode Island, Massachusetts, Connecticut
42 to 55 for tarot only. Eastern clock. Vermont and Maine are small, so their lead is shaky.
37, 35 and 32 for tarot. Huge numbers of people, ordinary interest per person.
agree: Most new-age states overall: Arizona, Nevada, Oregon, Utah, Colorado. Reiki is strongest in New England.
Cultural Currents Institute, 16 search words, Dec 2022 to Jan 2023
New York has the most 'psychic' searches per person; Rhode Island, New York and Massachusetts top the list overall
Duel.com study, as reported by Film Daily
states.akashic_warn: Weak: few searches, small states on top

clock.note: Evening (7 to 10 pm) in each place, shown in India time. Plain clock arithmetic for winter; whether evening is the best hour for this audience is not measured. From March to October the US, Canada, UK and Ireland rows fall one hour earlier in India time, and Sydney one hour later.

choice.title: The decision that comes before the country
a: The big audience above. English only. Our assumption, not measured: they know tarot well, Akashic a little, mulank not at all, and want reflection and clarity more than prediction.
b: About 57 lakh in the US, 36 lakh in Canada, 13 to 18 lakh in the UK, 10 lakh in Australia. Our assumption, not measured: they already trust tarot, numerology and Akashic, and Hinglish works. They earn in dollars and pounds.
choice.note: The two need different reels, language and prices, and the second makes the Gulf matter, where the legal risk is. Diaspora counts: Ministry of External Affairs, January 2025, as reported by Deccan Herald; the ministry's own table lists 17.6 lakh for the UK.

care: PayPal's Braintree lists fortune tellers among businesses it will not serve, and Stripe's restricted list names psychic services and fortune tellers. How an Indian seller gets paid from abroad for readings is not solved yet, and it can block the whole plan.
Do not sell into the UAE
UAE law punishes sorcery and quackery, and local guides say that covers fortune-telling and promoting it online. Other Gulf countries not checked.
New York makes paid fortune telling a misdemeanour unless it is presented as entertainment, and other states and towns have their own rules. Not checked state by state.
UK rules make the seller prove a claim: no accuracy claims, no promises on health, wealth or curses. Say guidance and reflection. This matches the page's own honesty rules.

Meta rejects ads that state or imply something personal about the viewer, such as health or money trouble. Hooks that work in reels may be refused as ads. The full list on Meta's page was not read in this pass.
Healing is never a medical claim
Readers abroad state on their booking pages that a session is not medical, legal or financial advice. Seen on listings; not a legal check.
open: How people abroad would pay, and which payment company will accept this kind of business from India. Must be answered first.
Which foreign pages already win with this content. No foreign tarot, Akashic or healing page has been scouted yet; that needs the Instagram browsing go-ahead.
Whether a new account posted from India gets shown to viewers abroad, and what helps. Not checked; no source read.
US rules state by state, and other Gulf countries. Only New York and the UAE were read.
How many searches these words get in each country (real volumes, not the 0 to 100 index). Not available free.
Whether Sakshi wants to speak on camera in English, Hinglish, or use voice-over. Her call.
The psychic-belief surveys for the UK (2011) and Canada (2016, 2021) are old. Nothing newer was found in this pass.
Not opened by the reviewer: IBISWorld, Similarweb, Angus Reid, the Australian sources, Duel.com, the diaspora counts, the Tarotoo article and the price listings.

review.verdict: Mostly sound. 'Indians abroad first' and 'no VPN, no borrowed number' are reasonable choices, but both were stated more firmly than the evidence allows.
notes: 25 points and 8 gaps raised; the must-fix ones are corrected on this page.
Corrected: 'the only lane with proof' was too strong. The proof is about big apps that buy customers with ads, not a single reader.
Corrected: the VPN answer is now a recommendation, not a fact. Only one Meta page was read and it lists some signals.
Corrected: Canada's province numbers mixed South Asian and Indian counts; payment and legal risks apply to both lanes, not only the Western one.
Corrected: the gates had no numbers. Pass marks are now set in step 2, and the Western test is counted by hand because Instagram shows country, not origin.
Added on the reviewer's advice: keep the new account apart from the Indian page; a step for language, first product, tax and refunds before the account opens.
Still open: the fixes have not had a second review. The reviewer could not open Instagram's Help pages and read the two Meta extracts as supplied.

plan.verdict: Start with Indians living abroad, but as a judgement to be tested, not a proven fact. The evidence is stronger there and the cultural fit is closer; neither lane has proof for a single reader selling from India. Treat Western seekers as a later test with a pass mark. What step 2 finds is allowed to change this choice.

lanes.name: Indians living abroad
lanes.line: Fewer people, better evidence that they pay Indian providers, closer fit to what Sakshi already does.
for: Astrotalk earned Rs 621 crore abroad in FY26, 34% of operating revenue, up from 20% a year before; the US gives more than 60% of it. Its founder named the Indian diaspora as the main source in an interview a year earlier; the FY26 figure itself is not split by customer group.
Inc42, 28 Oct 2026 and Inc42 feature; Open magazine. The founder is also quoted at 37% in one piece.
InstaAstro, which also sells tarot and numerology, reportedly gets about 25% of revenue from abroad, largely the diaspora.

They can afford it: Indian-headed households in the US earn a median 151,200 dollars a year, against about 83,700 for the US overall. This shows ability to pay, not willingness to pay a single reader.
Pew Research, 2023 data; US figure from an agency report
Sakshi's present product, a numerology report, and her way of speaking already fit this audience.

Some of them can pay the way Indian buyers do: NRIs in 12 countries, including the USA, UK, Canada and Australia, can use UPI with a foreign number, but only if they hold an NRE or NRO account at a bank that supports it, and only in rupees.
RBL Bank page (names the 12); NPCI page (no country list)
against: The proof is two venture-funded apps that buy customers with ads: Astrotalk spent Rs 823 crore on marketing in FY26 across India and abroad, about 45% of revenue. It does not show that one reader posting reels can do the same.

About 5.2 million in the US, 1.9 million in the UK, 1.3 to 1.9 million in Canada and 0.7 to 0.8 million in Australia: roughly 9 to 10 million. Each country counts differently (identity, ethnic group, origin, birthplace).
US Census via Pew; UK censuses 2021-22; Canada census as reported; Australian census

Hindi is the home language of under a fifth of Indian Americans (18%; Telugu 11%, Gujarati 10%, Tamil 7%). English is the only language that reaches nearly all: 84% are proficient. Many more may follow Hindi than speak it at home; that was not measured.
If this lane has to be in English, its reels overlap a lot with the Western lane. The two lanes are less separate than they look.

lanes.name: Western seekers
lanes.call: Later, only if it passes a test
lanes.line: Far more people, weaker evidence that an India-run page can sell to them, and less overlap with what Sakshi sells now.
for: 30% of US adults consult astrology, tarot or a fortune teller in a year: tens of millions of people. The US psychic services industry is about 2.3 billion dollars.
Readings abroad are listed at 60 to 395 dollars an hour.

Indian Akashic readers on Fiverr show buyers from the US, UK, Ireland and the Netherlands at 25 to 100 dollars. Weak, but it is the only evidence here about a single reader in India, which is Sakshi's case.
Fiverr listings: a hint, not proof of scale
against: Most Americans who do this say it is for fun: 20% for fun, 10% for insight.
Akashic is searched about a fifth as much as tarot. Mulank is, in our reading, unknown to this audience.
No source was found showing an India-based tarot or Akashic page earning from Western buyers at scale. Competition from local readers was not measured.

plan.second: Should the second lane be done at all? Not decided, and it should not be decided on opinion. Run it only after the first lane has made sales, as ten reels in plain Western English. Instagram's numbers show a viewer's country, not whether they are of Indian origin, so the test has to be counted by hand: paying enquiries from people who are plainly not of Indian origin. Write the pass number down before posting. If it is not reached, drop the lane.

reach.title: Reaching them from an India-run account
reach.answer: Our advice: no VPN and no friend's phone number. Run the account from India, openly. This is a recommendation from what was read, not a proven fact.
why: No evidence that the creator's connection decides who sees a reel

On the one Meta page read, the card for the reels shown after you open a reel, no listed signal is about the creator's location, SIM or number. The signals are about the viewer and the reel, such as how well it matches what the viewer watches. The card lists only some signals, and the cards for the Reels tab, Explore and Feed were not read. So this is 'no evidence it helps', not 'proved it does nothing'.
Meta Transparency Center, Instagram Reels chaining card, read 21 Nov 2026
The one country signal points at a different risk

The card lists 'how much time viewers from your country have spent on this reel'. Early watching by Indian viewers would then help a reel with Indian viewers, not foreign ones. That argues for keeping the new account away from the present Indian followers and phone contacts: no cross-promotion, contact syncing off.
Same card; the conclusion is the reviewer's and ours
Instagram may show where an account is run from

Instagram says it shows a country label on posts of 'certain accounts' based outside the place most of their audience is from, and that it works the country out from things including stated location, devices and connection. We cannot say whether a VPN would change that label. Hiding the country is pretending, on a feature made to show it.
A borrowed number has a plain cost
Whoever holds the number holds the account's recovery. And in our view, for a reader in India speaking to Indians abroad, being in India is part of the appeal, not something to hide.
levers: English as Indians speak it, with Hindi words where natural, if Sakshi is comfortable on camera in English. If not: voice-over, text reels, or Hindi with subtitles for the Hindi-speaking part.
Life abroad: visa and job worry, family far away, marriage pressure from home, festivals alone. Our assumption; untested.
Keep it apart from the Indian page
No cross-promotion, contact syncing off, a separate store or price page so buyers abroad do not see the Rs 555 price.

In winter 8:30 am IST is the previous evening in the US: 10 pm East, 9 pm Central, 7 pm West. From March to November it is an hour later there, so post an hour earlier. Whether the hour changes who sees a reel was not found in anything read.
Instagram's tool that shows a reel to non-followers first. Not for day one: a guide citing Instagram Help says a creator account needs 200 followers. Confirm in the Help Centre.
The only way to choose a country, state or city directly. Meta's ad tools accept countries, regions and cities. Costly in the US and subject to Meta's ad rules.
reach.note: Which of these matter most is our judgement, not a tested result. The first batch of reels is the test.

where.note: For the first lane the question is where Indians abroad live. You still cannot pick states when posting; this sets the clock, the references and any later ads.

steps.what: Find out if a buyer abroad can pay, and if the business is allowed
steps.how: Ask people in two countries (say the US and the UK or Canada) to buy through the present SuperProfile link by foreign card: the Rs 555 report, and one product priced in dollars. Ask SuperProfile in writing whether tarot, Akashic and healing sessions sold to buyers abroad are allowed. Cost: the price of the test purchases.
steps.gate: Money arrives from both countries and SuperProfile says yes in writing. If not, find another payment route before anything else. One friend's card is not proof that strangers' cards will work.

steps.what: Look at who already wins, and set the pass marks
steps.how: Scout 5 to 10 pages of single Indian readers and astrologers with an audience abroad, not apps. This is the only step that can show one reader earning from the diaspora. Needs the go-ahead for Instagram browsing at the agreed slow pace.
steps.gate: At least three pages named with what works for them, and the pass marks for step 4 written down from their numbers. If no single reader is found doing this, the lane choice is looked at again.

steps.how: Sakshi's call on English on camera. Choose what to sell first: a report needs no night hours, live readings for the US mean early mornings in India. Set a provisional price for abroad. Ask a CA about GST, export of services and bank paperwork. Write a refund policy.
steps.gate: Language, first product, provisional price and the CA's answer are written down.

steps.what: Open the new account, honestly and apart
steps.how: A creator account made in India on Sakshi's own phone and number. English bio that says who she is and where. Contact syncing off; nothing posted about it on the Indian page.
steps.gate: Account open. No VPN, no foreign number.

steps.how: About life abroad, with a clear offer and price, posted on the US evening over three weeks. Independent review before posting, as for all Tarot Talk work.
steps.gate: The step 2 pass marks: share of viewers abroad, and a counted number of enquiries from abroad. A new account may not show viewer countries until it has enough followers; if so, count from who comments and messages.

steps.how: Confirm the price for abroad from what the enquiries say. Indian sellers abroad list 25 to 100 dollars.
steps.gate: A set number of paid orders from abroad by a set date, both fixed in step 2.

steps.how: Only now use the state lists: small paid tests to California, Texas, New Jersey and Ontario, with a spending cap fixed first, if Meta approves the ads and the local rules for those places have been checked.
steps.gate: Cost per buyer is below what is left from a sale after fees, tax and Sakshi's time.

steps.how: Ten reels in plain Western English.
steps.gate: The hand-counted pass number of non-Indian paying enquiries is reached, or the lane is dropped.

open: Whether SuperProfile accepts readings sold abroad, and whether strangers' foreign cards go through. SuperProfile's own comparison page says buyers abroad can pay in 16 currencies while Indian creators are paid in rupees; its about page says only 'their own currency'. Not tested.
No single Indian reader's page with an audience abroad has been scouted. This is the biggest gap in the lane choice.
Why a new account and not an English series on the present page was not weighed with numbers. The country signal above is one reason for a new account; it is not proof.
Tax, GST and bank paperwork for money from abroad. Local consumer and advertising rules outside New York and the UK.
Meta's cards for the Reels tab, Explore and Feed, and Instagram's Help page on who can use trial reels, were not read.
Gulf countries stay out for both lanes until a lawyer says otherwise.

both.title: Risks that sit on both lanes
rows: Payment companies restrict this business: PayPal's Braintree bars fortune tellers and Stripe's restricted list names psychic services. Stripe in India is invite-only and not open to individuals. Whether SuperProfile allows readings sold abroad is not known.

New York requires paid fortune telling to be presented as entertainment, and New York is the largest Indian metro area in the US. Rules in other US states, the UK, Canada and Australia were not checked.
Tax, GST and bank paperwork for money from abroad were not checked. Refunds and card disputes need a written policy.
